name: Chesed
overview: Chesed is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as a son of Nahor. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide further details about his tribe or other distinguishing notes. His mention is brief and specific to his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Chesed appears as a proper name in Genesis 22:22. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to this name in the biblical text provided, so it is recognized simply as a personal name.
familyAndRelationships: Chesed is identified as a son of Nahor and Milcah, establishing his immediate family relationships. Scripture does not record additional family connections beyond these parental ties.
scriptureSignificance: Chesed's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement as a son of Nahor, who is a notable figure in the patriarchal narratives. This connection situates Chesed within the broader story of Abraham's family line, contributing to the understanding of the ancestral heritage in Genesis. Though not elaborated upon, his mention helps preserve the historical record of Nahor's descendants.
